report.source_text: In accordance with infectious disease consult, our patient underwent methyl prednisolone pulse therapy (1 g/d) for 3 days, and then prednisolone (1 mg/kg/d) as a maintenance therapy was initiated. Therefore, intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIg) (25 g/d for 5 days) was initiated for the patient, which resulted in the improvement of both mental state and clinical symptoms.

report.source_text: After 3 months of clinical follow-up, the patient was still blind (no light perception) without pupillary light reflex. Muscle forces returned to normal; nevertheless, a wide-based gait was still observed (which was not reliable due to blindness). MRI also showed no new lesions. Prednisolone was tapered (10 mg/d) and patient received warfarin (international normalized ratio 2.2).

clinician.trajectory_summary: A 49-year-old man presented with abrupt complete vision loss in his right eye and visual impairment in his left eye, along with moderate headache, three weeks after a confirmed COVID-19 infection. Initial brain MRI showed diffuse restricted bilateral foci in both parietal and occipital lobes, suggestive of acute infarction. CSF analysis was negative for common viral pathogens (HSV, VZV, SARS-CoV-2 PCR). The patient's vision deteriorated to complete loss in the left eye, and a repeat MRI revealed extension of infarct lesions. An occipital cortex biopsy showed brain tissue with focal infiltration of foamy macrophages, reactive astrocytes, and scattered CD3+ cells, without evidence of vasculitis or granuloma, indicating an inflammatory process. Treatment with methylprednisolone, prednisolone, and intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIg) led to improvement in mental state and other clinical symptoms, although blindness persisted. Follow-up MRI showed no new lesions.

key_supporting_evidence.claim: Patient presented with acute vision loss and headache following a confirmed COVID-19 infection.
Brain MRI showed diffuse restricted bilateral foci in parietal and occipital lobes, suggestive of acute infarction, which later extended to other brain regions.
CSF analysis ruled out common viral causes of encephalitis (HSV, VZV, SARS-CoV-2 PCR).
Occipital cortex biopsy revealed inflammatory changes in brain tissue, including focal infiltration of foamy macrophages, reactive astrocytes, and CD3+ cells, consistent with an inflammatory process.
Patient's clinical symptoms (mental state, hemiparesis) improved following immunomodulatory treatment with corticosteroids and intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIg).
